extracted.intended_audience: recipient organizations, institutional grants/offices, and PD/PIs who administer NIH grants
extracted.subtask_description: Post-award terms, conditions, and management standards that NIH-funded recipients must follow for research products, financial and property management, procurement, monitoring, and reporting. Covers expectations for interim products, internal controls, program income, property, and progress reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Research Products — public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the product publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH intends to maximize impact of interim research products developed with NIH funds and expects recipients to ensure a high level of public access; preprints are a common form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Research Products — licensing preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a Creative Commons Attribution (CC-BY) license or dedicate work to the public domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH strongly encourages CC-BY or public-domain dedication to maximize impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Research Products — in-text disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: In the text of the document: acknowledge NIH funding; clearly state that the work is not peer-reviewed; declare any competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow acknowledgement guidance in NIH GPS Section 8.2.1; declare competing interests as an author would for any journal article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Research Products — standardized terms and responsible norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standardized terms of use to facilitate text mining and adhere to norms of responsible scientific communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH expects standardized terms of use and adherence to other norms of responsible scientific communication when claiming an interim product as NIH-supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient systems/policies/procedures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient organizations are expected to have systems, policies, and procedures in place to manage funds and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may use existing systems provided they are consistently applied regardless of fund source and meet 2 CFR Part 200 and NIHGPS standards; NIH may review adequacy and take action as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls — establishment and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and maintain effective internal controls to provide reasonable assurance of compliance with Federal statutes, regulations, and award terms (2 CFR 200.303(a) and (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must evaluate and monitor compliance (2 CFR 200.303(c)) and take prompt action when noncompliance is identified (2 CFR 200.303(d)). Internal controls should align with 'Standards for Control in the Federal Government.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes of conduct expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish codes of conduct defining integrity, ethical values, and personnel competence criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes should assure compliance with award terms including providing true, complete, and accurate application information; safe, non-discriminatory work environments; and meeting public policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management system standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet standards and requirements for financial management systems set forth in 2 CFR Part 200.302 as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must provide assurance funds are used appropriately, maintain adequate transaction documentation, and safeguard assets; NIH requires accounting/internal control systems to monitor grant accounts and identify large unobligated balances, accelerated expenditures, inappropriate cost transfers, and other inappropriate obligations/expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient notification of problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify NIH when financial management problems are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A failure to establish adequate control systems is a material violation and may prompt NIH to add specific award conditions or enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income — definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Program income is gross income earned by a recipient, consortium participant, or contractor directly generated by the grant-supported activity or earned as a result of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes fees for services, rental charges for grant-acquired property, sale of fabricated items, charges for research resources, registration fees for grant-supported conferences, license fees and royalties on patents and copyrights; licensing/royalty income from copyrighted material/patents generally exempt from reporting unless specified in award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income — accountability and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH applies the additive alternative to all recipients unless concerns or program requires different alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may require a different program income use if recipient has deficient systems, history of large unobligated balances, or multiple final budget period extensions; program income may only be used for allowable costs under applicable cost principles and award terms; NoA will indicate allowable treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting program income
rubrics_metrics.description: Report amount of program income earned and amount expended on the appropriate annual financial report (FFR); report program income in the Program Income section (lines 10 L–O).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deduct any costs associated with generating gross program income that are not charged to the grant to report net program income. For SNAP awards, report program income in the non-competing continuation progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income alternatives (Additive/Deductive/Combination/Matching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and applicability of program income alternatives: Additive, Deductive, Combination, Matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additive: added to funds and used to further project objectives; Deductive: deducted from total allowable costs to determine net allowable costs for Federal share; Combination: additive up to $25,000 then deductive for excess; Matching: used to satisfy non-Federal share. Additive applies to all NIH awards unless concerns exist; Deductive/Combination/Matching available on exception basis or where program requires matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale of real property/equipment/supplies — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for sale of real property, equipment, and supplies depend on grant type and recipient; some non-profit recipients are exempt from accounting to NIH for proceeds, but NIH retains certain rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment/supplies acquired for basic/applied research by nonprofit IHEs or research nonprofits are exempt from proceeds accounting, but NIH may require transfer of title for equipment costing $10,000+ under 2 CFR 200.312; other recipients follow 2 CFR 200.313/200.314 for use/sale of unused supplies; proceeds may need to be credited or paid per award instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalties and licensing fees reporting — inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Income from royalties or licensing fees from NIH-funded inventions and patents must be reported per Bayh-Dole implementing regulations (37 CFR Part 401.14(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual invention utilization report must include income generated by all subject inventions to which title has been elected and by certain licensed research tools even if not patented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property management system standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use their own property management policies, provided they observe regulatory requirements in 2 CFR Parts 200.310–200.316 and additional NIH-specified standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State governments follow state laws (45 CFR Part 92.32). Dollar thresholds for equipment applicability are based on unit acquisition cost; accessories and fabricated property treatment described; recipients must be prudent—conduct prior review to ensure necessity and inability to meet need with existing property; obtain prior approval when required; follow procurement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and supplies — title and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Title to equipment and supplies acquired with NIH funds generally vests in the recipient, subject to property management requirements; limited exceptions exist (States and exempt property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements do not apply when only depreciation/use allowances are charged, for donated equipment, or equipment acquired primarily for sale/rental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt property — NIH right to require transfer for $10,000+ items
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may require transfer of title to equipment with acquisition cost of $10,000 or more to the Federal government or eligible third party within specified conditions (2 CFR 200.312).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may exercise this right within 120 days of award completion/termination or within 120 days of receipt of an inventory, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonexempt property — full regulatory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonexempt equipment and supplies are subject to the full range of acquisition, use, management, and disposition requirements in 2 CFR Part 200.313 and 200.314, and internal control requirements in 2 CFR Part 200.303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such property must not be encumbered without NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment management system minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Management system for equipment must include adequate records, periodic physical inventory, control procedures, maintenance procedures, and proper sales procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must identify items and current location; physical inventory at least once every 2 years (sampling acceptable); safeguards to prevent loss/damage/theft; regular maintenance; proper sales procedures when authorized to sell equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition rules for equipment $10,000+
rubrics_metrics.description: For equipment having unit acquisition cost of $10,000 or more, NIH may require transfer of title or issue disposition instructions; if IC fails to issue instructions within 120 days, recipient may sell and reimburse NIH an amount equal to NIH's percentage share of current market value or proceeds (recipient may retain $1,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If instructed to ship, awarding IC reimburses recipient by applying recipient's share percentage to current fair market value plus shipping/storage costs; net amount may be used for the project if project still receiving support and NIH approves; otherwise remit net amount by check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual inventory of unused supplies > $10,000
rubrics_metrics.description: If residual inventory of unused supplies exceeds $10,000 in aggregate fair market value at termination/completion and supplies are not needed for other federally sponsored programs, recipient may retain or sell but must compensate the awarding IC for its share as a credit to the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unfair competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not use equipment acquired with grant funds to provide services for a fee to compete unfairly with private companies unless award terms provide otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocable license conditions for federally owned tangible personal property
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocable license agreement conditions: title remains with Federal government; NIH may require return if in the Federal government's interest; use must not permanently damage property; property must be controlled and maintained per 48 CFR Part 45.5 (FAR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to make federally owned personal property available to recipients for the period of grant support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement system standards — applicable regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must follow procurement requirements in 2 CFR Part 200.318 through 200.327 (States may follow their own policies but must include required clauses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party activities involving programmatic work are addressed under Consortium Agreements chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts under grants — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract under a grant must be a written agreement stating activities to be performed, time schedule, applicable policies and requirements (including 2 CFR Part 200 Appendix II clauses), maximum liability, and cost principles for cost-type contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract must not affect recipient’s overall responsibility and must reserve sufficient rights and control to the recipient to enable fulfillment of responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-type contracts spanning budget periods — charging conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient may charge costs of a service-type contract to the budget period in which executed even though services occur in a succeeding period if certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: awarding IC has been made aware at application or post-award; project recommended for a project period extending beyond current year; recipient has legal commitment to continue the contract for full term. Costs allowable only for services provided during NIH support; recommended clause for contracts of $100,000 or less to make payment beyond current budget period contingent on continued Federal funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement approval requirements — NIH discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may require prior approval of specific procurement transactions if certain circumstances exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances include: noncompliant procurement procedures; procurement expected to exceed simplified acquisition threshold (~$250,000) awarded without competition or with only one bid; procurement specifies a brand name; proposed award over threshold to other than apparent low bidder in sealed-bid procurement; contract modification changes scope or increases amount by more than simplified acquisition amount. When prior approval is required, recipient must provide sufficient information for review; NIH approval does not legally endorse the business arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small/minority/women/veteran-owned business contracting efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make positive efforts to use small businesses, minority-owned firms, women's business enterprises, and veteran-owned businesses as sources of goods and services whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should take steps outlined in 2 CFR Part 200.321 to implement this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic preferences for procurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient or subrecipient should, to the greatest extent practicable and consistent with law, provide a preference for goods/products/materials produced in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of this section must be included in all subawards, contracts, and purchase orders under Federal awards; see 2 CFR Part 200.322.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring — NIH oversight activities
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH awarding ICs monitor grants via review of reports and correspondence, audit reports, site visits, and other available information to identify potential problems and provide technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring continues as long as NIH retains a financial interest in the project (may continue after administrative closeout for property/audit/other requirements). Names and phone numbers of monitoring contacts provided at award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting — periodic financial and progress reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must periodically submit financial and progress reports and other required reports (annual invention utilization, lobbying, conflict of interest, audit reports, payment reports, specialized programmatic reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients expected to publish results in peer-reviewed journals and provide information to the public on objectives, methodology, and findings; GMO is official receipt point for most reports; annual progress reports centralized; eRA Commons required for some reports and closeout documents; failure to submit complete/accurate/timely reports may lead to closer monitoring, award delays, or enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Competing Continuation Progress Reports — RPPR use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) must be submitted and approved by NIH for non-competing continuation funding of each additional budget period within a project period (Type 5 progress reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except SNAP awards, progress report includes updated budget; NIH requires RPPR for Type 5 including accessing Human Subjects System link where applicable; late submission delays issuance/funding and may reduce award amount; recipients must submit complete and accurate reports and provide additional information if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commons ID requirement for RPPR participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons ID is required for PD/PI(s) and those in postdoctoral roles for progress reports using the RPPR; Commons ID required for undergraduate and graduate students supported on the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate Student and Postdoctoral eRA Commons Roles should NOT be used for individuals submitting Individual Fellowships or trainees on institutional training grants (use PD/PI or Trainee roles respectively). Commons ID optional but encouraged for other project personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation for Individual Development Plans (IDPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions are encouraged to implement an institutional policy requiring an Individual Development Plan (IDP) for every graduate student and postdoctoral researcher supported by any NIH grant and reportable on the progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report implementation in RPPR Section B. Accomplishments, Question B.4 (report IDP use for graduate students/postdocs in RPPR Section D Participants or on Statement of Appointment Form PHS 2271). Do not include the actual IDP; provide information describing how IDPs are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP — Streamlined Non-Competing Award Process applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: SNAP modifies annual progress reports, Notices of Award (NoAs), and financial reports for certain awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards routinely included in SNAP are 'K' and 'R' awards (except R35). Awards excluded from SNAP include those that generally cannot automatically carryover unobligated balances (centers; cooperative agreements; institutional training grants; non-Fast Track Phase I SBIR/STTR awards), clinical trials (regardless of activity code), P01, R35, and awards to individuals, although inclusion/exclusion can be grant-specific. Awards may be excluded for close monitoring needs or recipients with poor reporting/notification histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP — modified annual progress reports and NoAs
rubrics_metrics.description: SNAP awards use a streamlined version of the RPPR that does not include detailed budget information and have modified NoAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The streamlined RPPR replaces the eSNAP module in eRA Commons.
